measurements.source: Per sample, one-core-equivalent percent = (whole-process user+system CPU milliseconds / workload wall milliseconds) * 100. It may exceed 100% when multiple threads run simultaneously. Host-normalized percent divides that value by os.availableParallelism(), the OS-reported available parallelism at capture time; it is not a machine-wide OS utilization reading.

measurement.workerStartup: Worker constructor through ready handshake; separate from workload wall and CPU time
measurement.processCpu: process.cpuUsage delta for the whole Node process during journaled workload; includes CPU used by scenario Worker threads and the RSS monitor thread; worker startup CPU is reported separately
measurement.cpuUtilization: Per sample, one-core-equivalent percent = (whole-process user+system CPU milliseconds / workload wall milliseconds) * 100. It may exceed 100% when multiple threads run simultaneously. Host-normalized percent divides that value by os.availableParallelism(), the OS-reported available parallelism at capture time; it is not a machine-wide OS utilization reading.
measurement.effectiveWorkerCount: Concurrency is capped at 4; the pool is limited to four Workers, available parallelism, and the scenario count.
measurement.percentile: Batch p95 uses nearest-rank from 5 independent measured batches per concurrency; fewer than 30 samples are provisional.
measurement.peakRss: Independent Worker thread polls process.memoryUsage.rss() every 5ms nominally; each sample also records the largest observed gap, making practical timer scheduling resolution explicit. RSS is process-wide and sampled rather than a hard peak guarantee.
measurement.rssLimit: Not a hard total-process memory limit: worker old-generation caps do not cap young generation, native allocations, main thread, monitor thread, or process RSS; do not sum RSS values or per-worker caps as a total-process bound.
measurement.endToEndTime: worker startup + workload wall + worker shutdown; serial is workload wall only
